what_this_is: The Workshop rows for tools/meaning-search: the package's find-similar-vector and find-similar actions on the person's own index descriptor and vector set, the same question over several descriptors, the words said in a set's lines, and the builders of a vector set.

payload.label: Find what is closest to a vector
payload.job: Find the moments in my recordings, pictures or documents closest in meaning to a query vector, such as the picture vector of some words, and say the file and time of each
payload.description: Runs meaning-search's find-similar-vector on one of the person's semantic-index-descriptor records: the descriptor's vector set (items and their vectors, two of the person's files) is indexed by the package's own scripts for the run, the ANN index narrows the candidates and the exact cosine ranks them, best first, never padded below the descriptor's min_score. query_vector_base64 is base64 of JSON {"vector": [...]} made by the model the descriptor names (tool:words-as-picture-vector gives one for words when the set holds picture vectors). Returns index_id, model_id, model_version, result (items with address, score, revision and payload_hash; considered, skipped, min_score) and points_to (each address's file, start, end and text). With spread ({per_file, seconds_apart}) the answer holds at most per_file items of one file, that far apart, so many neighbouring frames of one take do not fill it.

index_id.description: The index_id of one of the person's semantic-index-descriptor records

query_vector_base64.description: base64 of JSON {"vector": [...]}, made by the model the descriptor names

limit.description: At most this many items; the descriptor's result_limit caps it

spread.description: Keep one recording from filling the answer: best first, an item is set aside when its file already has per_file items in the answer or one closer than seconds_apart to it (an item with no time counts once per file). The package ranks up to the descriptor's result_limit, then the answer is cut to limit; result.spread says how many were set aside.

payload.label: Find what is closest in meaning to some words
payload.job: Find the moments in my recordings or documents whose words or transcript are closest in meaning to what I ask, and say the file and time of each
payload.description: Runs meaning-search's find-similar on one of the person's semantic-index-descriptor records: query_text and any item of the vector set without a vector are embedded by the descriptor's model at its model_endpoint (the package's Ollama embedder), the set is indexed for the run, the ANN index narrows the candidates and the exact cosine ranks them, best first, never padded below the descriptor's min_score. Returns index_id, model_id, model_version, result (items with address, score, revision and payload_hash; considered, skipped, min_score) and points_to (each address's file, start, end and text). With spread ({per_file, seconds_apart}) the answer holds at most per_file items of one file, that far apart, so many neighbouring frames of one take do not fill it.

index_id.description: The index_id of one of the person's semantic-index-descriptor records

limit.description: At most this many items; the descriptor's result_limit caps it

spread.description: Keep one recording from filling the answer: best first, an item is set aside when its file already has per_file items in the answer or one closer than seconds_apart to it (an item with no time counts once per file). The package ranks up to the descriptor's result_limit, then the answer is cut to limit; result.spread says how many were set aside.

payload.label: Make a searchable set of what my videos show (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Turn a folder of my videos into a set of picture vectors, one frame every few seconds with its time, so I can find moments by what they show
payload.description: Reads every video in a folder the person names (only reads it) and keeps one frame every few seconds (2 by default), decoding key frames only, small, with an optional 3D LUT for log footage and an optional smaller proxy copy on the same timeline to decode instead. Each frame becomes a CLIP ViT-B-32 picture vector (OpenAI weights, the model tool:words-as-picture-vector uses for words, so they compare). Writes the two files of a vector set, frames.npy (float16, normalised) and frames.jsonl (video, path, t in seconds, the file decoded), with done.json so a run that stops goes on where it stopped and a new card adds only its videos, and vector-set.json: the vector_set member to put in the person's semantic-index-descriptor record so tool:find-similar-to-a-vector can search it. It runs on the person's own computer, never on Trillion.

input.description: The folder of videos on the person's computer, put where {input} is in the command.

output.description: The folder of the vector set, put where {output} is in the command; the same folder again adds new videos to it.

output_schema.description: The last line the script prints: {"result": {"frames", "added", "videos_done", "out"}}. {output}/vector-set.json holds the vector_set member for the descriptor and the model that made the vectors.

get_it: python3 -m pip install -U numpy torch open_clip_torch pillow
needs: model: CLIP ViT-B-32 with the openai weights (MIT licence; open_clip downloads them on first run)
invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, never on Trillion. If you can run commands where they are: check whether it is already installed, install it with get_it if not, ask which folder of videos (add --pattern '*.MP4' to take only some files, --lut FILE.cube when the footage is log, --proxy '{dir}/../SUB/{stem}S03.MP4' or the like when the camera wrote smaller copies, --every N for a frame every N seconds), run `run`, and tell the person how many frames were added. It can run for hours on a large card; run it again to go on. Then put vector-set.json's vector_set, with the model it names, into a semantic-index-descriptor record of theirs and search it with tool:find-similar-to-a-vector (words become a query vector through tool:words-as-picture-vector). If you cannot run commands, give them these steps.

provenance.source: ffmpeg and open_clip (https://github.com/mlfoundations/open_clip) CLIP ViT-B-32 openai weights

payload.label: Find what is closest to a vector across several of my indexes
payload.job: Find the moments across all my recordings and pictures, kept in several indexes, closest in meaning to a query vector, best first across all of them, and say the file and time of each
payload.description: Runs meaning-search's find-similar-vector on each of several of the person's semantic-index-descriptor records (index_ids) and merges their answers by score, best first. The indexes must come from one model (a picture index and a speech index, or two models, are refused: their scores do not compare). With spread ({per_file, seconds_apart}) the merged answer holds at most per_file items of one file, that far apart. query_vector_base64 is base64 of JSON {"vector": [...]} made by the model the descriptors name (tool:words-as-picture-vector gives one for words). Returns index_ids, model_id, model_version, result (items with address, score, revision and payload_hash; considered and skipped summed over the indexes, min_score) and points_to (each address's file, start, end, text and any field the descriptor's points_to.carry names, such as a readable name).

index_ids.description: The index_id of each of the person's semantic-index-descriptor records to search together

query_vector_base64.description: base64 of JSON {"vector": [...]}, made by the model the descriptor names

limit.description: At most this many items; the descriptor's result_limit caps it

spread.description: Keep one recording from filling the answer: best first, an item is set aside when its file already has per_file items in the answer or one closer than seconds_apart to it (an item with no time counts once per file). The package ranks up to the descriptor's result_limit, then the answer is cut to limit; result.spread says how many were set aside.

payload.label: Find the lines my recordings say, by their words
payload.job: Find the spoken lines in my recordings that say all of some words, and say the file and time of each
payload.description: Reads the vector sets of several of the person's semantic-index-descriptor records (index_ids) whose points_to names a text field, and returns, in the order the sets hold them, the lines that contain every word of query_text longer than two letters (case ignored), at most limit (8 when none is asked). Needs no model: it matches the words themselves, where tool:find-similar-by-meaning matches what they mean. Returns index_ids and lines: each line's address, file, start, end, text and any field the descriptor's points_to.carry names.

index_ids.description: The index_id of each of the person's semantic-index-descriptor records to search together

query_text.description: The words to look for; every word longer than two letters must be in a line

limit.description: At most this many lines (8 when none is asked)

payload.label: Make a searchable set from picture vectors another program kept (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Turn picture vectors my programs already kept (an asset index of CLIP matrices, a folder of timed frames, an app's results store) into sets I can search by what the pictures show
payload.description: Reads, only reading, the stores the person names: an asset index of CLIP matrices (video frames with no time, images, and readable names from assets.jsonl), a folder of timed frames (frames.npy and frames.jsonl), and an app's SQLite results store of timed frames (base64 float16 vectors, each item's path from its library entries), with the id a namespace store keeps each of those videos under. Each store becomes its own set in --out: items.jsonl (path, kind, t or null, and name, or id and b2), vectors.npy (float16, normalised) and vector-set.json, the vector_set member of a semantic-index-descriptor record with points_to.carry naming the extra fields. Last line: {"result": {"sets": {name: items}}} or {"error": ...}.

input.description: For matrix: the .npy file. For results-db: the results store file. Put where {input} is in the command.

output.description: The folder of the vector set, put where {output} is in the command.

output_schema.description: The last line the script prints: {"result": {"items", "out"}}. {output}/vector-set.json holds the vector_set member for the descriptor.

invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, never on Trillion. Give each store they keep: --asset-index (a folder of clip-video-embeddings.npy, clip-video-ids.json, clip-embeddings.npy, clip-ids.json and assets.jsonl), --ssd-index (frames.npy and frames.jsonl), --expansion-results (an app's results store of timed frames) and --namespace (a namespace store, so each Expansion item carries its b2 id); --kind video, image or all. Each store becomes its own set in --out. The model of the vectors must be the one the person's search words are turned into vectors with (tool:words-as-picture-vector); say which model the descriptor names. Then put each vector-set.json's vector_set, with that model, into a semantic-index-descriptor record of theirs and make the two files readable to their AI through their files. If you cannot run commands, give them these steps.

provenance.source: ffmpeg and open_clip (https://github.com/mlfoundations/open_clip) CLIP ViT-B-32 openai weights
